I'm confused, you need to save the webhook in the config entries as you'd need to re-use it later on?

How is removing it prevent issues with the cloud hooks?

Previously, we stored both the webhook_id and generated webhook_url in the config. This resulted in webhooks failing when users changed the external URL or enabled/disabled nabu.casa. Even though the component's webhook sync with Withings occurs every 2 hours (and on startup), the user's changes would have no effect because the config's webhook_url is what was sent to Withings.

This change only persists the webhook_id. When the component's webhook sync runs, it will generate the webhook url and pass that to Withings. This ensures Withings is regularly updated with the correct webhook url instead of a persisted one.

It should not generate a new one... that is the whole point.

See for example Netatmo or Toon integrations on how to handle this correctly.

@frenck I see both those integrations persist the cloudhook url in the config entry. Why is that? What if the user deletes their cloud account and creates a new one? How would we update the URL for the new cloud account? I tend to think that generating a new webhook/cloudhook on config entry setup would be most flexable.

> I tend to think that generating a new webhook/cloudhook on config entry setup would be most flexable.

That is simply not allowed, it will create a lot of webhooks, that is not needed.

> I see both those integrations persist the cloudhook url in the config entry.

Yes, it should.

> Why is that? What if the user deletes their cloud account and creates a new one? How would we update the URL for the new cloud account? 

It stores the webhook ID, not the URL. Hence it is not an issue. The ID is used to generate the URL, which means the registered webhook is re-used. For cloud it will result in the same URL (unless account is changed). For local, it will result in the same URL (unless URL settings are changed).

@frenck Could you provide some clarity on the comment above? The examples you mention both persist the cloudhook url. If you change nabu casa accounts, these integrations would need to be removed and added in order for them to use a different account.
@frenck Could you provide some clarification to the above comment?

> @frenck Could you provide some clarity on the comment above? The examples you mention both persist the cloudhook url. If you change nabu casa accounts, these integrations would need to be removed and added in order for them to use a different account.

Yes, at this point, you are correct. However, that is a small case, which should not be solved on the integration level. For the future, we should look into getting a helper that does all this magic (for both cloud and local).
